messages:
noah: After installing redwoodctl in a debug container I hit a perpetual auth refresh loop when LOCALTEST=1. It writes tokens then immediately 401s.

anya: which package/installer? apt, brew, release tarball?

noah: tarball unpacked to /opt/redwoodctl, added to PATH. Container runs as UID 1000 but the tarball install steps ran as root earlier in Dockerfile.

raj: may be ownership/umask issue. If token file is created by root with mode 600 and later process as user can't read it cleanly, it could reattempt refresh.

noah: logs (sanitized):
```
INFO auth: start device flow
DEBUG tokens: write /home/app/.redwood/tokens/default.json uid=0 mode=0600
INFO api: POST /token -> 200
INFO token: saved
INFO api: POST /token -> 401 invalid_grant
ERROR auth: refresh failed
INFO auth: retrying
```

anya: confirms root wrote the token. When process runs as non-root later it may see stale file or fail to atomically replace, leading to inconsistent reads.

raj: quick fix: ensure install step ends with chown -R 1000:1000 /home/app/.redwood and set umask 0027 so files are readable by the user. Also check if entrypoint uses su -c vs gosu which preserves env.

noah: workaround: in entrypoint I added `if [ $(id -u) -eq 0 ]; then chown -R $(id -u app):$(id -g app) /home/app/.redwood || true; fi` then redwoodctl login --device. Fixed loop.

cli-bot: tip: use REDWOODCTL_TOKEN_DIR to point to a writable path under /tmp for ephemeral CI runs.

anya: product note: we should make CLI warn when tokenfile owner != effective uid and when umask would prevent token overwrite. Also ignore overlay refresh_token in LOCALTEST mode to avoid silent loops.

devex-bot: created issue #2722: "redwoodctl: warn on token ownership/umask mismatches; ignore overlay refresh_token in localtest; doc entry for container installs" (assigned devex).

noah: I'll attach Dockerfile and logs to #2722 and open a small PR for the entrypoint snippet.
